identity.title: ALMA chemical survey of disk-outflow sources in Taurus (ALMA-DOT). II. Vertical stratification of CO, CS, CN, H<SUB>2</SUB>CO, and CH<SUB>3</SUB>OH in a Class I disk

paper_type_evidence.quote: we observe the edge-on disk around the Class I source IRAS 04302+2247 (the butterfly star) in the 1.3 mm continuum and five molecular lines.

evidence.quote: located in Taurus ($d=161\pm3$ pc, (cite: galli19))
edge-on disk ($i = 90\pm3\degree$[^1], (cite: wolf03))
located in Taurus ($d=161\pm3$ pc, (cite: galli19))
edge-on disk ($i = 90\pm3\degree$[^1], (cite: wolf03))

question.value: How are CO, CS, H2CO, CN and CH3OH distributed vertically in the edge-on Class I disk of IRAS 04302, and what is the CH3OH/H2CO abundance ratio?

evidence.quote: We report the first tentative detection of methanol (CH$_3$OH) in a Class I disk and resolve, for the first time, the vertical structure of a disk with multiple molecular tracers.
project 2018.1.01037.S, PI: L. Podio
Observations were taken with ALMA-Band 6 on October 28, 2018

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: High-resolution (0.141 MHz) SPWs covering CO 2-1, CN 2-1, o-H2CO, CS 5-4, CH3OH; CS in broad continuum SPW (1.129 MHz)

evidence.quote: The correlator set-up consists of high-resolution (0.141 MHz) spectral windows (SPWs)
with baselines ranging from 15 m to 1.4 km
The clean beam of the self-calibrated maps ranges from 0.31$''$$\times$0.26$''$ to 0.41$''$$\times$0.32$''$
the root mean square (r.m.s.) noise per channel is $\simeq 0.8-2.3$ mJy beam$^{-1}$
The integration time sums up to $\sim 113$ minutes.
Observations were taken with ALMA-Band 6 on October 28, 2018
(PI L. Podio)

what.value: Molecular line parameters (spectroscopy) for column densities

evidence.quote: converted into column densities through the molecular parameters in Table [\[tab:lines\]](#tab:lines) (cite: Mueller2005)

what.value: Comparison CH3OH/H2CO ratios for TW Hya, HD 163296, hot corinos, comets

evidence.quote: $\sim 1.27 - 1.73$ for T$_{\rm ex} \sim 25-75$ K, (cite: walsh16; carney19)

evidence.quote: Data reduction was carried out using CASA 4.7.2.

self_calibration.value: Self-calibration on continuum, applied to line-free continuum and continuum-subtracted line; continuum S/N improved by 3.4

evidence.quote: The signal-to-noise ratio (S/N) of the continuum improved by a factor of 3.4 after the self-calibration.
The final maps were produced with TCLEAN

weighting_robust.value: robust=0.0 for CO, H2CO, CS, CN; robust=2.0 for CH3OH

evidence.quote: We used Briggs weighting with robust=0.0 for the bright CO, H$_2$CO, CS, and CN lines
by applying a manually selected mask on the visible signal
$\simeq 0.8-2.3$ mJy beam$^{-1}$

evidence.quote: The validity of these assumptions is discussed by (cite: podio19).

analysis_steps.goal: Image continuum and line cubes, moment maps

evidence.quote: Moment 0 and 1 maps were produced over the velocity range \[$+1.2, +10$\] km s$^{-1}$, except for CO

method.value: Profiles across disk height from moment 0 maps, averaged over three pixels (0.18")

evidence.quote: by averaging the emission radially over three pixels (0.18$''$, corresponding to $\sim 29$ au)

validation.value: Errors as standard deviation over a nine-pixel box

evidence.quote: The errors in the figure correspond to the standard deviation obtained over a nine-pixel box.

method.value: Integrate over molecular layer (A=4.3 arcsec2) and outer midplane (A=0.41 arcsec2); convert to N

evidence.quote: The column densities of the detected molecular species were inferred by assuming local thermodynamic equilibrium and optically thin lines.

key_parameters.value: Noise = sigma0*sqrt(A/theta_beam); upper limits at 3 sigma

evidence.quote: The noise on the line integrated emission is $\sigma_0 \times \sqrt{A/\theta_{\rm beam}}$
The total H$_2$CO and CH$_3$OH column densities were derived assuming an ortho-to-para ratio of $1.8-2.8$

validation.value: A posteriori check that CH3OH intensity is consistent with expected abundance ratio

evidence.quote: the integrated line intensity is consistent with the expectations for the \[CH$_3$OH\]/\[H$_2$CO\] abundance ratio
Data reduction was carried out using CASA 4.7.2.

findings_qualitative.value: CN does not show an X-shape and is detected at constant height above the midplane

evidence.quote: the CN $2-1$ emission does not show an X-shape and is instead detected at a constant height above the midplane

claims.hypothesis: Molecules are vertically stratified in the disk
claims.result: z/r 0.41-0.45 for CO vs ~0.2-0.28 for CS and H2CO
claims.finding: CO traces higher layer; CS and H2CO cospatial

evidence.quote: CO observed at larger disk heights (aperture $z/r \sim 0.41-0.45$) compared to both CS and H$_2$CO

claims.hypothesis: CH3OH is present in a Class I disk

evidence.quote: therefore, this is a 3$\sigma$ detection

claims.hypothesis: H2CO is released from icy grains in the midplane
claims.result: H2CO drops only a factor ~2 vs >100 for CO and 15 for CS
claims.finding: Consistent with formation on ice and nonthermal release

evidence.quote: which is possibly due to H$_2$CO formation on icy grains, followed by a nonthermal release into the gas phase

limitations_admitted.value: No estimates of disk temperature, so Tex assumed

evidence.quote: As there are no estimates of the disk temperature, the excitation temperature is assumed to be 20$-$100 K

referee_caveats_inferred: Tex assumed, large column density ranges
LTE and optically thin assumed for CS, H2CO

reproducibility.score_reason: Data identified and imaging parameters partly given, but several processing and region details missing.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Key CH3OH result is marginal and region definitions are incomplete.
